inputs.name: servers
inputs.description: Host to run the Zabbix server and frontend on, by name: a map of one name to an address, or to a host object with an address and optional host_key, user, port, private_key_file, jump_hosts or os. Empty for agents that report to a server you run elsewhere.

inputs.name: agents
inputs.description: Hosts to run Zabbix agent 2 on, by name, in the same form as servers. Each name becomes the agent's Hostname, the name you give the host in Zabbix. A name can be in both servers and agents, so the server monitors itself.

inputs.name: zabbix_version
inputs.description: Zabbix release and package revision to install, as Zabbix's Debian packages number them, such as "7.0.32-2". The release's first two numbers pick Zabbix's repository. Raising it upgrades every Zabbix package in place.

inputs.name: database
inputs.description: PostgreSQL database the server and frontend keep their data in. The role and an empty database it owns must exist, such as from circuit-postgres. The defaults suit PostgreSQL on the server host itself.

inputs.name: database_password
inputs.description: Password of the database user. Needed with servers. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_database_password; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password to give the frontend's Admin user in place of Zabbix's default, zabbix. When null, Admin keeps whatever password it has. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_admin_password; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address the frontend listens on. The default keeps it to the server host itself, for a reverse proxy or an SSH tunnel in front.

inputs.name: listen_port
inputs.description: Port the frontend serves on, in plain HTTP.

inputs.name: server_address
inputs.description: Address the agents know the server by: they accept passive checks from it and send active checks to it. When null, the address of the host in servers.

inputs.name: agent_psk
inputs.description: Encrypt the agents' traffic with a pre-shared key. Each agent generates its own key, which never leaves the host; you register it with the server yourself. See the README.
